title: Diversity of Group B Streptococcus Serotypes Causing Urinary Tract Infection in Adults

claims.text: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) was cultured from 1.1% of consecutive adult urine samples (387/34,367).
claims.byte_quote: GBS was cultured from 387/34,367 consecutive urine samples (1.1%)

claims.text: Serotypes V, Ia, and III caused the most GBS UTIs.
claims.byte_quote: Serotypes V, Ia, and III caused the most UTIs

claims.text: Serotypes V, Ia, and III together account for 76% of the 62 GBS UTI cases.
claims.byte_quote: The most prevalent serotypes among the 62 cases of GBS UTI were serotypes V, Ia, and III (Table 2), which together account for 76% of cases.

claims.text: Nontypeable GBS was not associated with UTI.
claims.byte_quote: Nontypeable GBS was not associated with UTI.

claims.text: GBS UTI case patients were significantly older than controls (mean 53 vs 30 years).
claims.byte_quote: the mean age of case patients was significantly greater (53 ± 19 years versus 30 ± 12 years; P < 0.001)

claims.text: Prior history of UTI raised the odds of GBS UTI (OR 3.1).
claims.byte_quote: GBS UTI case patients were significantly more likely to have had a prior history of UTI than controls (OR, 3.1; 95% CI, 1.1 to 8.7)

claims.text: Female sex raised the odds of GBS UTI (OR 3.8).
Women of child-bearing age with GBS UTI were less likely to be pregnant than child-bearing-age controls (37.5% vs 81.4%).
claims.byte_quote: Significantly fewer women of child-bearing age (defined as <40 yrs) with GBS UTI were pregnant than women of child-bearing age who were controls (37.5% [6/16] versus 81.4% [35/43]; P = 0.003)

claims.text: Confirmed GBS UTI cases (31/62 with urinalysis) all had positive leukocyte esterase and pyuria.
claims.byte_quote: All 31 of the 62 patients who had UA performed had positive results based on positive urinary leukocyte esterase and pyuria

claims.text: GBS isolates were uniformly susceptible to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, penicillin, linezolid, and chloramphenicol.
claims.byte_quote: they were uniformly susceptible to amoxicillin (amoxicilline) with clavulanic acid, penicillin, linezolid, and chloramphenicol

claims.text: A substantial proportion of GBS isolates were resistant to clindamycin (26.4%) and erythromycin (39.5%).
claims.byte_quote: A considerable proportion of isolates was resistant to clindamycin (102/387 [26.4%]) and erythromycin (153/387 [39.5%])

claims.text: Most GBS isolates were resistant to tetracycline (80.4%), cefoxitin (88.7%), and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (98.3%).
claims.byte_quote: the majority was resistant to tetracycline (311/387 [80.4%]), cefoxitin (343/387 [88.7%]), and trimethoprim with sulfamethoxazole (380/387 [98.3%])

claims.text: Only one GBS UTI patient had concurrent GBS bloodstream isolation, indicating probable urosepsis.
claims.byte_quote: only one patient had GBS concurrently isolated from blood, representing probable urosepsis
